**Scores** of youths in Kashmir have been booked under the stringent **Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA)** for allegedly participating in protests following the death of **Ayatollah Ali Khamenei**, the Supreme Leader of **Iran**.  The arrests have sparked concerns from **National Conference (NC) legislators** who met with **Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha** on Sunday, March 15, 2026. The NC delegation demanded the withdrawal of these cases before the upcoming religious holiday of **Id**.  They argue that the arrests are disproportionate and may be counterproductive to achieving peace in the region.

The **NC memorandum**, signed by several legislators including **Tanvir Sadiq** and **Hilal Akbar Lone**, highlights that while mourning gatherings for **Khamenei** have been held peacefully across India, individuals in **Kashmir** are facing criminal charges under the UAPA and the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)**. The memorandum emphasizes that these arrests set a concerning precedent by targeting mourners for expressing grief.  The NC leaders also point out the lack of legal action against similar gatherings held in other cities across India, arguing that this disparity undermines equal citizenship and protection under the law.

**Sinha**, listening to the demands of the delegation, promised to review the cases before **Id**. He assured the legislators that he would ensure the release of those arrested for participating in these mourning gatherings. The NC leaders expressed hope that these arrests will be withdrawn.

recent_articles.rephrased_article:
## Former Kashmir Chief Minister Targeted in Shooting Attempt

Jammu and Kashmir Police have formed a seven-member Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate the attempted assassination of former Chief Minister Farooq Abdullah. The incident occurred on Wednesday night at a marriage function in Greater Kailash, where Abdullah was leaving when a gunman opened fire on him from behind.  The 63-year-old suspect, identified as Kamal Singh, was apprehended immediately and a revolver used in the attack was recovered from his possession. Inspector General of Police Bhim Sen Tuti ordered the formation of the SIT due to the "seriousness and sensitivity" of the case.

## Ladakh Protests Continue Despite Climate Activist's Release

Despite the release of climate activist Sonam Wangchuk from detention, protests planned for Monday in Ladakh are still expected to go ahead.  The Leh Apex Body (LAB) and the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), representing the region's districts, have maintained their demands for constitutional safeguards including Statehood, inclusion under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution, a Member of Parliament for each district, and filling government vacancies. They argue that meetings with the Union Ministry of Home Affairs have not yielded any concrete results.  While the revocation of Wangchuk's NSA detention is welcomed, protests will continue as planned, with organizers expecting 1,000 participants in Kargil on Monday.  Opposition parties are criticizing the BJP-led government for the prolonged detention and questioning the use of laws like the NSA.
